## Intent
Hypothesis: a Halide-expressible branchless blend with per-particle hash RNG and no intermediates can approach the streaming ceiling on identity-ordered particles.

## Cache saturation
At N=4000 (above L1d spill at 963, below L2 spill at 61680), ns/p is 11.759 at q=0.01 — per-frame setup overhead dominates. By N=16000 cost drops to 8.139 as overhead amortizes. Crossing the L2 spill at N≈61680 to N=65000, cost stays FLAT at 7.989 — no knee. From N=262000 through N=4000000 (DRAM-resident), cost remains flat at ~7.95–8.0. Death rate does not change the N-shape; q=0.25 is slightly faster (7.67–7.75) than q=0.01 (7.95–8.0), suggesting dead particles skip render work.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 8.87 GB/s at N=16000, q=0.25 — 35% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. At q=0.01, peak is 8.56 GB/s (34%). Bandwidth is flat from N=16000 onward, never climbing as the working set enters DRAM. This is compute/overhead-bound, not bandwidth-bound: a streaming-limited kernel would approach 25 GB/s at large N. The transition is by N — overhead-bound at N=4000 (5.78–6.37 GB/s), settling by N=16000 into a plateau at ~8.5–8.9 GB/s that persists to N=4M.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize the render loop. Only 2 vector-suffixed instructions appear in 354 (`movi.2d v1`, `movi.2d v3`, both zeroing); `ldr q0` loads a constant in setup. The hot loop at 0x100057230 uses scalar `s`-registers: `ldp s4, s5`, `ldp s6, s7`, `ldr s16`, `fadd s4`, `fmul s4`, `fsub s4`, `fcvtzs`. No gather is present. Render writes are byte-granular scatters — `strb w2, [x1]`, `strb w2, [x1, #0x1]`, `strb w2, [x1, #0x2]`, `strb w11, [x23, x0]` — four byte stores per particle with `csel` clamping (18 total). Walk1 is delegated to `_halide_b1` via `bl`; its codegen is not shown. The scalar loop and byte scatter explain the 35% cap.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo never exceeds 8.87 GB/s (35% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling) because the render pass's byte-granular `strb` scatter stores cannot stream and the per-particle loop runs in scalar `s`-registers with no vectorization. Flat ns/p from N=16000 through N=4M confirms compute-binding, not bandwidth-binding.
